rv.q: Now that such moral entropy is a working daily assumption, it might be time for a version in which Piggy and Ralph are given bigger rhetorical weapons against the depravity of their peers.
Golding’s exploration of society, civility, order and acceptance is all brought to thrilling life by an extraordinary cast of young men, many making their professional stage debuts.
Anthony Lau’s overwrought production takes a symbolic approach to William Golding’s classic
Blending thrilling movement, lighting, and sound choices with the actions of the cast, Lau and the performers have you transfixed through the highs and lows of the action throughout the two halves.
A flawed, concept-driven production, it is given force by the sheer quality of the young actors.
I regret I cannot be more positive about this show.

cn.t: Anthony Lau's stark, stripped-back production divides critics. While some praise its timely resonance and searing intensity, others find Nigel Williams's 1995 adaptation inadequate, questioning whether it captures the full cruelty of Golding's vision.
